subject: Provisional capacity haircut request & GPU-price hedge ask for Lumina
summary: Lumina requests a 12-month reserved commit with an option for a provisional capacity haircut tied to GPU market moves. Sales seeks approval for a deal-level discount and a price-protection clause; ops needs confirmation on activation windows and fallback model variants.
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire@lumina.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Patel <jason@lumina.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal + ask about price protection

Evelyn,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. We liked the Dedicated proposal and are close on terms internally. Two asks before we move to signatures: 1) can Redwood support a provisional haircut if GPU market prices spike (we need a trigger to reduce committed hours temporarily) and 2) is there flexibility on the committed discount if a haircut is exercised? We are planning for a 12-month term, target commit 60k GPU-hours/month (Aurora-style V100 equivalent) but want a way to limit our downside if GPU prices jump >12% quarter-over-quarter.

Attached: SOW draft v3 and our internal costing notes.

Next steps for us: confirm the coverage corridor and discount band, then legal will circulate PO.

Best,
Claire
Claire Thompson
Head of AI Ops, Lumina Health

+1 415 555 0192

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Jason Patel <jason@lumina.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal + ask about price protection

Claire — thanks for the clear asks. High level we can support a provisional haircut and a price-protection/hedge mechanism but need to align commercial guardrails and ops constraints. Quick answers: 

- Coverage corridor: we can offer a 12-month reserved commitment with two activation tranches (0-6 mo, 7-12 mo) and allow a one-time provisional haircut of up to 25% of committed monthly hours if a pre-agreed GPU price index moves >15% (quarter).
- Discount: up to 18% off list for the baseline commit; if the haircut is exercised we propose a partial rollback to a 12% discount for the months affected to preserve capacity economics.
- Approval path: discounts >15% require finance + VP sign-off; any change to the discount during the term requires a contract amendment via DocuSign.
- Ops: we need sizing confirmation for burst-to-on-demand and preferred fallback model families (quantized variants).

I'll loop in Jonas for the discount approval and Marcus for the activation mechanics. Marcus — can you confirm the feasibility of the 2-tranche activation and a one-time 25% haircut from an ops capacity perspective?

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Jonas — ops notes on the proposed construct: 

- Two-tranche activation is fine; we will reserve the full pool but gate activation windows to avoid fragmentation. Tranche A (baseline) kicks at contract start; Tranche B is time-locked to month 7 and subject to utilization thresholds (we'll include a 60% utilization trigger).
- One-time haircut up to 25%: technically feasible but requires explicit fallbacks: 
  * fallback to a compatible, quantized model family we maintain (e.g., q4 variants) to reduce price sensitivity, or
  * temporary migration to on-demand with a pre-agreed uplift for the months of the haircut if we need to free physical GPUs for higher-priority workloads.
- We need to lock the allowed model families and quantization level in the SOW to protect scheduling.
- Attach pricing_workbook_lumina.xlsx with the estimated op cost delta for a 25% haircut applied months. See the "ops-impact" tab.

I'll coordinate with capacity planning to ensure activation won't conflict with other reserved pools in Q1. If Lumina wants a deeper hedge (indexation + escrow), that'll need finance sign-off.

Marcus Lin
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity proposal + ask about price protection

Team — commercial view and approval ask: 

- Straight discount request: baseline 18% off list for the committed 60k GPU-hours/month is within our pricing bands, but any reduction of the discount during term (12% fallback during haircut months) must be explicitly documented.
- Approval thresholds: finance will approve up to 16% via delegated authority; anything >16% requires VP Sales approval. Kimberly — can you approve up to 18% for this deal given strategic value and likelihood of expansion?
- Hedge option: Lumina asked for a market-triggered haircut. We can implement a simple index linked trigger (3-month trailing average GPU spot index >15% increases) and a one-time haircut with the 12% discount rollback. For anything more complex (escrow, indexed credits), we need legal & finance to sign off and it will delay close by ~2 weeks.

If Kimberly approves the 18% and the index-triggered one-time haircut, I'll draft the commercial clause language for legal.

Jonas Weber
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the thread and the clear options. I'm comfortable approving an 18% baseline discount for Lumina given the strategic pilot and expansion signals. Conditions I want in the final SOW: 

1) One-time provisional haircut up to 25% allowed only if the index trigger (3-month trailing GPU spot >15%) is met and Lumina confirms in writing the month they want to exercise it.
2) During haircut months discount reverts to 12% (documented formula).
3) Activation tranches and allowed fallback model families must be enumerated in the SOW (Marcus, work with legal to lock model family names).
4) Any request for repeated haircuts or an escrow arrangement requires Exec-level sign-off and will be considered a contract amendment.

Evelyn — please push the clause language to legal and counter with Lumina. Jonas — once you draft the clause I can sign off in writing.
